The story is a meditative, original piece of writing that avoids overused expressions, predictable plot points, and stock characters. Instead of relying on dramatic cliches (such as a miraculous last-minute rescue, a dying message, or melodramatic grief), the narrative treats the discovery of the crash with quiet realism and contemplative restraint. Furthermore, the prose uses fresh, inventive figurative language—such as describing a bent guardrail "the way wire bends when a man has decided to give up on the fence," a heartbeat as a chest "making its small argument for going on," and the wind sounding "like water moving through a house where nobody lived anymore"—rather than relying on worn-out idioms.
